New pill cuts heart attack risk in trial, but experts urge caution

A once-daily pill made by Veltrix Pharmaceuticals lowered the risk of heart attack by 18 percent in a two-year trial, researchers reported Tuesday.

"This is a meaningful step for patients who can't tolerate statins," said Maren Okafor, a cardiologist at Lakeside University. Okafor added that the results still need to be replicated.

Dr. Tobias Wren, an epidemiologist at the Northfield Institute of Public Health, was more cautious. "The absolute benefit is small," Wren said.

The trial was funded by Veltrix Pharmaceuticals.
